papers.summary: Based on the analysis of 96 organizational innovation in healthcare (OIH) projects and 52 interviews conducted with project leaders initiating these innovations, this research identifies the phenomena underlying the genesis of OIHs. The results highlight the major role played by factors such as patient empathy, international inspiration, academic inspiration, technological inspiration, serendipitous encounters, and the desire for organizational transformation in driving the generation of OIHs. Furthermore, our findings emphasize the dual nature of the research and development process for these innovations, characterized as both ex nihilo and ex materia.

papers.summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. The analysis highlights the crucial interactions between internal and external dynamics, identifying essential conditions for successful innovations: effective mobilization of internal resources, robust institutional support, and early and active user involvement. However, the study also identifies limitations in citizen engagement, particularly in the evaluation phase of innovations. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

papers.authors: Christophe Maurel, Christophe Favoreu, London Proofreaders
papers.summary: This exploratory research aims to characterize, on the one hand, the concept of environmental management control (EMC) through the practices that underpin it, and, on the other hand, the tensions associated with it and the implementation of these practices in public organizations. Although EMC is attracting growing interest within the public sector, it seems to be facing technical and governance difficulties. A grid for analyzing management tools and the theory of organizational paradoxes is used to address the issue of characterizing EMC practices and the associated tensions in the local public sector. Various municipalities were mobilized to explore and characterize their first experiences of implementing EMC. Our results enable us to characterize both the tools used and the tensions generated between the objectives pursued in terms of resource management, dialogue with the socio-economic environment, and behavioral orientation.

papers.summary: Carbohydrate binding proteins (CBPs) are alluring and challenging targets in biology. CBPs achieve high-affinity interactions with their substrates through multivalent interactions with carbohydrates, often in branched, heterogeneous structures. Many cell recognition events and host-pathogen interactions are mediated by these carbohydrate-protein interactions. Therefore, the development of glycan-based mimics and disruptors of these interactions have applications in studying target CBPs, carbohydrate-based vaccines, immunomodulating agents, diagnostics, and therapeutics against cancer and other diseases. Previously, the Krauss lab has developed SELection with Modified Aptamers (SELMA), to evolve nucleic acid-scaffolded glycan clusters to develop high-affinity aptamers towards CBPs. Herein, I describe the extension of Hairpin-SELMA to fully 2′-modified RNA scaffolds, which confer enhanced serum stability, using engineered polymerases (KOD-DGLNK, SFM4-3, and Therminator).
